- The rating checks out on nVent's own sheet for SLK15L2SE250: 1.5 mm electrogalvanized wire, a 1/4 in stud, 44 lb static at 5:1, cULus.
- The same sheet gives 'Screw Length (L) 1 in' (25.4 mm). Its drawing and photos show the stud on a flat round eye, with a crimp sleeve below the eye and the wire leaving the sleeve. It has no hex.
- The CAD draws something else (crystal.py:244, :541-547): a 1/4-20 thread 12 long (tapped 13), under a round Ø9 x 16 body with an 8 hex at its bottom, sunk in a Ø10 bore 16.5 deep, its top 0.5 under the hub's face.
- The note says 'the stud's length and its body's size are not on the sheet'. That is wrong for the length.
- Scaled from nVent's drawing (the sheet gives no body sizes, so UNVERIFIED), the eye is about 14 to 18 across and the sleeve about 20 to 25 long: about 60 mm of rigid end in all.
  - It cannot enter a Ø10 bore.
  - The hub is only 41.5 tall (z 60 to 101.5).
  - Screwed in from the face, the eye and sleeve would stand to about z 140: through the crown's floor and above the cap's top (126) in today, A and B.
- Even the drawn fitting cannot be tightened. When its thread starts (16 below the face), its hex is already 0.4 to 4.4 down the Ø10 bore, and it ends 12.5 to 16.5 down. The hex corners are 0.38 from the bore wall, and an 8 socket coming from above cannot pass the Ø9 body. So 'turned by its hex, Loctite 243' can only be done by twisting the 2 m wire.
The suspension's lower end still has no anchor that can be built.
Fix: choose an end fitting whose shape its maker publishes and design the seat to that shape. For example, a swaged stop end bearing under a counterbore in the hub needs no turning. Or use the SLK's stud where nVent intends it, in the structure at the canopy, with a stop end at the hub. Draw the fitting as it is, and keep the pull test.

  - At the 9.0 lift the 30 deg turn needs 20.34, so the drawn tether goes taut at 27.4 deg, and the shade cannot be lowered at all.

  - The BOM's 'rated well over 10 x the 1.1 kg shade' is not backed by any part.
  - A tether's job is to catch a drop through its slack, which loads it far more than the shade's static weight (UNVERIFIED).

  - DIN 444 eye screws start at M5 (search result; the standard was not opened), so an M3 eye is a non-standard part.

- The swap text the build ships (crystal.py:1070-1073) still reads 'lift, turn, lower it off ... No tools', with no unclip step.
- The hook can only be reached inside the collar's bore, 4 above the lip and about 35 below the collar's top, past the carrier through a 13 mm annulus. It would be easier at the hub's end, which is in the open once the shade is lowered.
Fix: give the length (about 110 or more) and draw the slack; name a rated hook and eye; turn the hub's eye at least 40 deg away from the tab; add the unclip step to NOTES_DOME.

crit.verdict:
Not ready: two blockers in the suspension. The CAD does not draw the nVent anchor the note names (its sheet shows a 1 in stud on a flat eye and crimp sleeve, about 60 mm rigid, which cannot seat in the hub or fit inside any of the three tops), and the drawn hex cannot be reached by any tool. The canopy end is still not drawn, and as written its locks collide with the driver box and do not fit the canopy.
The rest works or needs small fixes: all three still come off (gaps unchanged), hang level at 1.64 deg per mm, the screws clear the studs and the cap is keyed. Should-fix: the tether (too short as drawn, unrated hook), the ring's lead-in lost in the solid, today's thin cap, and stale BOM rows and texts.

Yes, A. I checked these reasons myself on the committed v5 files.

1. A is the only top that answers both halves of his question: one tier fewer than today and B, and every tier the same.
- On the 1.8x crops (5.56 px per mm), A's three tiers come to about 63 rows each and the foot ring to about 61. So A reads as four bands within 4 % of each other.
- B's tiers are about 47 rows against the same foot (1.28 times), so it reads as five bands, like today.
- My per-row widths (py/bands.py) agree within a few rows.

2. A's cap is the better part to make (py/caps_check.py).
- Its Ø56 cap has 9.3 mm of metal outside both cable holes and 13 mm outside the dowel and magnet.
- B's cap has no cable holes, and its wires pass 0.75 mm outside it. Its dowel and magnet holes leave 1.0 mm of metal, 0.17 mm at the seat, and break out at the rounded bottom edge.

3. What A costs is small and stated correctly.
- It hangs 81 g more than today (1679 g against 1598 g; B 1577 g).
- It shows about 1.09 times today's black in the level views (B 1.00; py/black_top.py).
- Its collar, clamp, crown and cap cost $221.71, against $216.72 for today and $218.55 for B.

Three cautions:
- The thread is not a reason. A has 6.68 mm (4.5 turns) of full thread and B 3.85 mm (2.6), but the thread carries only the clamp's preload, which either length holds many times over. Do not put it to the owner as sturdiness.
- B has the better handle. At the 9.0 lift its Ø56 tier stands clear, while A's Ø80 tier leaves 1.84 mm beside a 1 mm gap. A's cap is still a fair handle, keyed by its dowel and both wires, so this does not change the pick.
- The runner-up's 'the wider spacing would cost B nothing more' goes too far. At 35 apart, B's wires hug its cap; at 50 to 60 they would stand about 8 to 13 mm off it. And the Ø62 hub has no room for the Ø10 stud bores at r 25 to 30 (1 mm of wall or less).
